summary: Gone Monroe County, Indiana, tower said to have been 80 feet, credited to the Kurtz CCC camp; still standing in 1952; only base corners remained at a 2023 visit.

facts.design: Said to have been an 80-foot tower (Forest Service list); no other design detail in the sources read
facts.status_note: Not standing; all four base corners exist per the 2023 visit. The Forest Service list says the footers are still visible.
facts.agency: Brownstown Ranger District, Hoosier National Forest

access.note: On public Hoosier National Forest land, with no road or parking at the site; visitors park briefly on the road and walk.

visit.trail_note: The 2023 visit walked to the site. The old forest road is not marked on the current Pleasant Run unit map.

events.note: Picture of the tower from 1947, part of a Hoosier National Forest historical marker near Leavenworth

Dutch Ridge Fire, placed in a broom sedge field near Bartlettsville at 1:15 p.m. on Sunday, October 26, 1952; reached within half a mile of the Dutch Ridge oil wells; a reporter tried to climb the tower during the fire

A September 4, 1963 item quoted by Forest Lookouts lists the replacement of the Dutch Ridge fire tower with a new $14,000 tower among recreation projects. The item does not say whether the replacement was built.
Visit in 2023: not standing; all four base corners present; no road or parking at the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts names Jackson County in its header beside the Brownstown Ranger District name. The Forest Service list and Indiana Fire Towers both place the tower in Monroe County, and the coordinates fit Monroe County. The story and the record use Monroe.

notes_for_editor: Built year is not in any source read. The CCC attribution comes from a Forest Service PDF about the Hickory Ridge tower and the Kurtz camp, so the story gives it as a credit, not a date. The 1952 fire section relies on a Forest Service fire-history PDF; a search summary said no fire account mentions the tower, but that PDF does (the reporter's climb), so the summary was wrong. The 1963 replacement item is unresolved: no source says whether a new tower was built, and the 2023 visit found only base corners. The story does not claim it was built. Staffing and fire-lookout operators are not named in any source read, so the story omits staffing. The Indiana Fire Towers 1947 picture is not added to photos because no license is stated. Read budget ran over (about 9 page reads including grep retries) because early greps returned truncated text. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the Monroe County and southeast-of-Bloomington location (Indiana Fire Towers), the Hickory Ridge CCC wording (Forest Service PDF), and the 1963 Republic item details were confirmed against the cached pages and added to evidence. The 1952 standing claim rests on the reporter's climb during the fire, which implies the tower was still up.
